comparison.objective: Candidate commissions and locks a robot-axis shock absorber through iterative physical impact tests; pr-1865 turns a cabinet hinge side cam to equalize door reveals, then closes/releases the door.
comparison.physical_skill: Both require tool alignment and controlled rotation, but the candidate adds recessed hex-key engagement, setscrew unlock/relock, collar counterholding, bimanual stabilization, bounded tightening, guarded cycle actuation, and adjustment from dynamic stopping response. pr-1865 uses a slotted screwdriver on one cam, avoids decoy screws, and closes the door to inspect static alignment.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two repeatable ≥0.85 J impacts at 0.3–3.30 m/s without exceeding 12 mm stroke, hard-stop contact, overload, excessive rebound, or lock drift. pr-1865 requires closed, even 3–6 mm reveals with ≤1 mm difference, ≤0.6 mm proud, no ≥1.2 mm sag, stillness and release for 1 s. Candidate does not yet declare numeric rebound, overload, or drift tolerances; that is a rubric gap but does not make these unrelated outcomes duplicates.
comparison.reason: The shared generic primitive—engaging and rotating an adjuster—does not establish overlap. The tested ability is meaningfully different: dynamic damper tuning and retention under repeated impacts versus static cabinet-door geometric alignment. All five available pr-1865 spec versions were read and describe the same objective and scoring family.
